title: Shared decoder with K-entry Mirror or latent function codebook
hypothesis: For 16 continuous functions, a K=16 codebook of two-angle Mirror views matches continuous latent2 normalized reconstruction RMSE within 10% at lower actual payload bytes, while K=4/8/16 sweeps quantify the quality/storage cost of fewer logical codes; compare to matched ordinary latent codebooks at each K.
mirror_coordinate: K learned two-angle hidden Givens codes and one quantized code index per function
logical_multiplicity: 16 function realizations selected from K codebook entries

task.teacher: random weighted Fourier sums with frequencies 1, 2, 3

success_gate: At K=16, Mirror codebook RMSE <=1.1x continuous latent2 RMSE and Mirror actual payload bytes are lower; compare matched-K ordinary latent codebooks and show the K-dependent function-quality frontier.
failure_gate: K=16 misses quality/bytes or a matched-K ordinary latent codebook matches or beats Mirror at comparable bytes.
boundaries: K entries do not imply K useful independent functions; report reconstruction and code use.
Fixed-update screen, not near-converged capacity evidence.
